studies.Title: Energy restriction in childhood and adolescence and risk of prostate cancer: results from the Netherlands Cohort Study.
studies.Reference: Energy restriction in childhood and adolescence and risk of prostate cancer: results from the Netherlands Cohort Study.
studies.Timing: Childhood exposure during 1944-1945 with 7.3 years of cohort follow-up through December 1993
studies.Population: Men aged 55-69 years enrolled in the Netherlands Cohort Study on Diet and Cancer
studies.comparison_type: Residence in a western Netherlands city during the 1944-1945 Hunger Winter versus the reference residence category

extraction_supporting_text.sample_size: The authors examined the hypothesis among 58,279 men aged 55-69 years enrolled in the Netherlands Cohort Study on Diet and Cancer.
extraction_supporting_text.cases: After 7.3 years of follow-up (through December 1993), 903 prostate cancer cases were available for analysis.
extraction_supporting_text.effect_size: The prostate cancer rate ratio for men who had lived in a western Netherlands city in 1944-1945 was 1.15 (95% confidence interval (CI): 0.80, 1.31), and the rate ratio for men who had lived in a western rural area in 1944-1945 was 1.30 (95% CI: 0.97, 1.73). Residence during the war years (1940-1944) and father's employment in 1932-1940 showed no relation to prostate cancer risk.
extraction_supporting_text.confidence_interval: The prostate cancer rate ratio for men who had lived in a western Netherlands city in 1944-1945 was 1.15 (95% confidence interval (CI): 0.80, 1.31), and the rate ratio for men who had lived in a western rural area in 1944-1945 was 1.30 (95% CI: 0.97, 1.73).
extraction_supporting_text.comparison: for men who had lived in a western Netherlands city in 1944-1945
extraction_supporting_text.continent: Netherlands Cohort Study on Diet and Cancer
extraction_supporting_text.exposure_measurement: Additional information was collected on residence during the Dutch Hunger Winter (1944-1945) and the World War II years (1940-1944) and father's employment status during the economic depression of 1932-1940, used as indicators of exposure.
